categories.name: AI app builders (free plans)
categories.intro: Where most AI-built apps start. The free plans are for trying, not launching.

categories.name: Hosting & deploy (free tiers)
categories.intro: Put your app on the internet. Read the terms: some free tiers do not allow commercial use.

categories.name: Databases
categories.intro: Where your users' data lives. Backups are usually the first thing a free tier leaves out.

categories.name: Auth & user accounts
categories.intro: Sign-up, login and user management. Free limits are counted in monthly active users.

categories.name: Email (transactional & marketing)
categories.intro: Password resets, receipts and newsletters. Daily send caps bite on launch day.

categories.name: File storage & media
categories.intro: Uploads, images and video. Bandwidth and operations cost more than storage.

categories.name: Monitoring, errors & uptime
categories.intro: Know your app is broken before your users tell you.

categories.name: Security & scanners
categories.intro: Free protection and free checks. Use them before real users and real data arrive.

categories.name: AI APIs
categories.intro: Free model access for prototypes. Rate limits and data-use terms matter more than price here.

categories.name: Analytics & SEO
categories.intro: See who comes, what they do and how Google sees you.

categories.name: Background jobs & cron
categories.intro: Scheduled tasks, queues and CI minutes.

categories.name: Forms, payments & support
categories.intro: The small pieces every launch needs.

entries.name: Lovable
entries.free: Free plan with free credit grants, up to 5 lovable.app domains and invite-only publishing (up to 10 invited people per project).
entries.hitsFirst: Public launch: free projects only open for people you invite, so going live to real users needs a paid plan.

entries.name: Bolt
entries.free: 300K tokens per day and 1M tokens per month, public and private projects, up to 3 collaborators.
entries.hitsFirst: The 300K daily token cap during long build sessions. Free sites also carry Bolt branding and uploads are capped at 10 MB.

entries.name: v0
entries.free: Free access to v0 with a 7-message-per-day limit, deploys to Vercel, visual Design Mode and GitHub sync.
entries.hitsFirst: 7 messages a day. Deploys land on Vercel Hobby, which Vercel's terms limit to personal or non-commercial use.

entries.name: Cursor
entries.free: Free plan with limited agent requests and limited chat requests (the pricing page does not publish a number).
entries.hitsFirst: Agent requests: a day of AI-assisted fixing uses up the free allowance; paid plans start at $8/month.

entries.name: Vercel (Hobby)
entries.free: 1M CDN requests, 100 GB Fast Data Transfer, 1M function invocations and 4 hours of Active CPU per month.
entries.hitsFirst: The terms, not the traffic: Hobby is for personal or non-commercial use only. Over a usage limit, that feature stops until 30 days have passed.

entries.name: Netlify (Free)
entries.free: 300 usage credits per month covering production deploys, compute, bandwidth, form submissions and web requests; 1 concurrent build.
entries.hitsFirst: The 300-credit hard cap: when one project reaches it, every project on the account is paused until the next cycle.

entries.name: Cloudflare Pages
entries.free: 500 builds per month, 1 build at a time, up to 20,000 files per site and 100 custom domains per project.
entries.hitsFirst: 500 builds a month if your AI tool pushes many small commits. Pages Functions count against the Workers Free limits.

entries.name: Cloudflare Workers
entries.free: 100,000 requests per day with 10 ms of CPU time per invocation; requests to static assets are not billed.
entries.hitsFirst: 10 ms of CPU per request: heavy server work (PDFs, image processing) fails. Workers Paid starts at $5/month.

entries.name: Render (Free instances)
entries.free: Free web services with 750 free instance hours per workspace per month, plus a free Postgres database.
entries.hitsFirst: Free services spin down after 15 minutes without traffic and take about a minute to wake; free Postgres databases expire 30 days after creation.

entries.name: Railway (Free)
entries.free: $1 of usage credit per month, services sleep and wake on request, up to 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB RAM per service and 0.5 GB volume storage. New accounts get a 30-day trial with $5 of credit.
entries.hitsFirst: $1 a month does not cover an always-on API plus a database; the Hobby plan is a $5 minimum.

entries.name: GitHub Pages
entries.free: Static sites from a repository: published sites up to 1 GB, a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month, 10 builds per hour (no build limit with a custom Actions workflow).
entries.hitsFirst: Usage policy: GitHub does not allow Pages for an online business, e-commerce or SaaS. Static files only, no server code.

entries.name: Firebase Hosting (Spark plan)
entries.free: 10 GB of hosting storage and 360 MB per day of data transfer at no cost, custom domain and SSL included.
entries.hitsFirst: 360 MB of transfer per day: one busy day with large images or video reaches it.

entries.name: Deno Deploy (Free)
entries.free: 1M requests and 20 GiB egress per month, 10 hours of Active CPU, 10 active apps, 5 custom domains, 1 GiB of KV storage.
entries.hitsFirst: Positioned for personal use and smaller projects; 1M requests per month and 15 builds per hour.

entries.name: Supabase (Free)
entries.free: Postgres with a 500 MB database, shared CPU / 500 MB RAM, 5 GB egress, 500,000 Edge Function invocations, 2 active projects.
entries.hitsFirst: Free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity, and automatic backups are not included. Daily backups start on Pro ($25/month).

entries.name: Neon (Free)
entries.free: Serverless Postgres: 100 projects, 100 CU-hours per project per month, 1 GB storage per project, scale to zero after 5 minutes, restore window up to 6 hours.
entries.hitsFirst: 1 GB of storage per project, and the first query after scale-to-zero waits for the database to wake.

entries.name: Turso (Free)
entries.free: SQLite-compatible: 100 databases, 5 GB storage, 500 million rows read and 10 million rows written per month, 1-day point-in-time restore.
entries.hitsFirst: 10 million row writes per month for write-heavy features (event logs, chat, analytics).

entries.name: MongoDB Atlas (M0 Free cluster)
entries.free: A free cluster with 512 MB of storage on shared RAM and vCPU.
entries.hitsFirst: 512 MB of storage, and shared resources mean slow queries under load.

entries.name: Upstash Redis (Free)
entries.free: 250 MB of data, 10 GB of bandwidth and 500K commands per month.
entries.hitsFirst: 500K commands per month: rate limiting or a session check on every request uses it up fast.

entries.name: Cloudflare D1
entries.free: SQLite at the edge: 10 databases, 5 GB total storage, 5 million rows read and 100,000 rows written per day.
entries.hitsFirst: Daily caps: once reached, queries return errors until the daily reset. Queries without indexes read many rows each.

entries.name: Cloud Firestore (Firebase Spark)
entries.free: 1 GiB stored, 50K document reads, 20K writes and 20K deletes per day, 10 GiB egress per month.
entries.hitsFirst: 50K reads per day: a feed or dashboard that re-reads whole collections on every page load burns through it.

entries.name: Pinecone (Starter)
entries.free: Vector database for AI search and RAG: up to 2 GB storage, 2M write units and 1M read units per month.
entries.hitsFirst: Read units once real users start asking questions; Supabase and Neon Postgres with pgvector are alternatives you may already have.

entries.name: Supabase Auth
entries.free: 50,000 monthly active users on the Free plan.
entries.hitsFirst: It lives in your Supabase project, so it pauses with the project after 1 week of inactivity.

entries.name: Clerk (Hobby)
entries.free: 50,000 monthly retained users per app, prebuilt sign-up / sign-in / profile UIs, up to 3 dashboard seats.
entries.hitsFirst: Fixed 7-day session lifetime and 1-day log retention; SSO and more controls are on Pro.

entries.name: Auth0 (Free)
entries.free: Up to 25,000 monthly active users, passwordless login, social connections, 5 organizations, 1 custom domain.
entries.hitsFirst: B2B needs: 5 organizations and basic attack protection only.

entries.name: Kinde (Free)
entries.free: 10,500 monthly active users, email, SMS and social login, MFA, organizations, custom domain, subscriptions & billing.
entries.hitsFirst: 10,500 MAU, the lowest user cap in this section.

entries.name: WorkOS AuthKit
entries.free: User management free for up to 1 million active users.
entries.hitsFirst: Enterprise single sign-on (SAML / OIDC) is billed per connection, usually the first paid line when you sell to companies.

entries.name: Neon Auth
entries.free: Managed Better Auth inside Neon, up to 60K monthly active users per project on Free.
entries.hitsFirst: Shares Neon's Free limits, including 1 GB of storage per project.

entries.name: Resend (Free)
entries.free: 3,000 emails per month, 100 per day, 3 domains, 30-day data retention.
entries.hitsFirst: 100 emails per day: a launch-day signup spike or a batch of notifications stops sending.

entries.name: Postmark (Developer)
entries.free: 100 emails per month on the free Developer plan, which does not expire.
entries.hitsFirst: 100 per month covers testing only; the next tier is 10,000 per month.

entries.name: Brevo (Free)
entries.free: Up to 300 emails per day once your account is approved for sending, plus a free SMTP server.
entries.hitsFirst: 300 emails per day: plan launch-day and newsletter sends around it.

entries.name: MailerSend (Free)
entries.free: 500 emails per month with email API, SMTP relay and drag-and-drop builder.
entries.hitsFirst: 500 per month: positioned for occasional testing and sending.

entries.name: Mailgun (Free)
entries.free: 100 emails per day, 1 custom sending domain, REST API and SMTP relay.
entries.hitsFirst: 100 per day and a single sending domain.

entries.name: Loops (Free)
entries.free: Up to 1,000 subscribed contacts, 4,000 marketing sends per 30 days, transactional sends included.
entries.hitsFirst: 1,000 contacts; free emails carry a 'Powered by Loops' footer.

entries.name: Cloudflare R2
entries.free: 10 GB-month of storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B operations per month; egress to the internet is free.
entries.hitsFirst: Class A operations (writes, lists) when an app uploads or lists many small files.

entries.name: Backblaze B2
entries.free: The first 10 GB of storage is free; free egress up to 3x your monthly storage.
entries.hitsFirst: Egress above 3x what you store, e.g. a small set of popular videos.

entries.name: Supabase Storage
entries.free: 1 GB of file storage with a 50 MB maximum upload size on the Free plan.
entries.hitsFirst: 1 GB total and 50 MB per file; file downloads share the project's 5 GB egress.

entries.name: UploadThing
entries.free: 2 GB of storage (shared between all your apps) and 7 days of audit log retention.
entries.hitsFirst: 2 GB shared across every app on the account.

entries.name: Cloudinary (Free)
entries.free: 25 credits per month and 3 users. 1 credit = 1,000 transformations or 1 GB of storage or 1 GB of image bandwidth.
entries.hitsFirst: Credits are shared across storage, bandwidth and transformations, so image-heavy pages use them fastest.

entries.name: Vercel Blob (Hobby)
entries.free: 1 GB of storage, 10K simple and 2K advanced operations, 10 GB of data transfer per month.
entries.hitsFirst: Same Hobby terms as Vercel hosting: personal or non-commercial use only.

entries.name: Sentry (Developer)
entries.free: 1 user, 5k errors, 5M tracing spans, 50 session replays and 5 GB of logs per month.
entries.hitsFirst: 5k errors: one noisy bug can use the whole month, and only one person can log in.

entries.name: Better Stack (Free)
entries.free: Free for personal projects: 10 monitors & heartbeats, 1 status page, Slack and email alerts, 100,000 exceptions per month, 3 GB of logs.
entries.hitsFirst: Logs and traces are kept for 3 days only.

entries.name: UptimeRobot (Free)
entries.free: 50 monitors at a 5-minute interval (HTTP, port, ping, keyword); personal and commercial projects allowed.
entries.hitsFirst: 5-minute checks: short outages can go unnoticed.

entries.name: Grafana Cloud (Free)
entries.free: All Grafana Cloud services with usage limits: 10k active metrics series, 14 days of retention for metrics, logs and traces.
entries.hitsFirst: 14-day retention and 10k active series once you add detailed metrics.

entries.name: Cloudflare (Free plan)
entries.free: DNS, unmetered DDoS protection, CDN, Universal SSL and the Free Managed Ruleset (WAF).
entries.hitsFirst: Meant for personal or hobby projects that aren't business-critical; no uptime SLA.

entries.name: Cloudflare Turnstile
entries.free: Free CAPTCHA alternative that blocks bots on signup, login and contact forms.
entries.hitsFirst: It only works if your server verifies the token on every submit; the widget alone protects nothing.

entries.name: GitHub secret scanning & Dependabot
entries.free: Dependabot alerts on every plan; secret scanning and code scanning are on by default for public repositories.
entries.hitsFirst: Private repositories need paid GitHub Secret Protection / Code Security for secret and code scanning.

entries.name: Snyk (Free)
entries.free: Dependency, code, IaC and container scanning: 200 open-source tests, 100 code tests, 300 IaC tests and 100 container tests per month.
entries.hitsFirst: 100 code tests per month if you scan on every push.

entries.name: Semgrep (Free Edition)
entries.free: Code and supply-chain scanning at $0 for up to 10 contributors.
entries.hitsFirst: The 10-contributor cap as the team grows.

entries.name: Gitleaks
entries.free: Open source (MIT): scans your whole git history for leaked API keys, locally or in CI.
entries.hitsFirst: It finds leaks; rotating the keys and cleaning history is still on you.

entries.name: ZAP
entries.free: Free, open-source web app security scanner (Apache-2.0).
entries.hitsFirst: Takes setup and judgement to read results; only scan apps you own.

entries.name: MDN HTTP Observatory
entries.free: Free scan and grade of a live site's security headers, no account needed.
entries.hitsFirst: Headers only: it can't see auth bugs, open database tables or leaked keys.

entries.name: Qualys SSL Labs Server Test
entries.free: Free online deep analysis of your HTTPS / TLS configuration.
entries.hitsFirst: TLS only; your hosting provider usually gets this right already.

entries.name: Google Gemini API
entries.free: Free tier on selected models with rate limits; some of the newest models are paid-only.
entries.hitsFirst: Data use: on the free tier your content is used to improve Google's products, so don't send customer data. Then rate limits.

entries.name: Groq
entries.free: Free plan with per-model limits on requests and tokens per minute and per day.
entries.hitsFirst: Requests per day on the model you picked; check the limits table before you build on one model.

entries.name: OpenRouter
entries.free: 25+ free models from 4 free providers behind one OpenAI-compatible API (model IDs ending in :free).
entries.hitsFirst: Free-model requests are capped per minute and per day; the daily cap rises after you buy credits.

entries.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
entries.free: 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge on both Free and Paid Workers plans.
entries.hitsFirst: The daily Neuron allowance (resets 00:00 UTC); beyond it you need Workers Paid.

entries.name: PostHog
entries.free: Every month: 1M analytics events, 5K session recordings, 1M feature-flag requests, 100K exceptions; 1 project, 1-year retention.
entries.hitsFirst: 5K session recordings once you have real traffic.

entries.name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
entries.free: Free, privacy-first, lightweight web analytics.
entries.hitsFirst: Traffic stats only: no funnels or per-user product analytics.

entries.name: Vercel Web Analytics (Hobby)
entries.free: 50,000 events per month with a 1-month reporting window.
entries.hitsFirst: At 50,000 events collection pauses; Hobby teams can't buy more.

entries.name: Umami Cloud (Hobby)
entries.free: Up to 100K events per month, 1 website, 6 months of data retention.
entries.hitsFirst: One website per account.

entries.name: Microsoft Clarity
entries.free: Free heatmaps and session recordings; Microsoft states there are no limits on traffic.
entries.hitsFirst: Recordings can capture what users type: mask sensitive fields and update your privacy policy.

entries.name: Google Analytics
entries.free: Free web and app analytics; event-level data is kept for 2 or 14 months (2 by default).
entries.hitsFirst: The 2-month default retention: switch it to 14 months on day one.

entries.name: Google Search Console
entries.free: Free service from Google: search queries, impressions, sitemap submission and indexing issues for your site.
entries.hitsFirst: Data only: it tells you what's wrong, fixing it is up to you.

entries.name: Upstash QStash (Free)
entries.free: HTTP message queue and scheduler: 1,000 messages per day.
entries.hitsFirst: 1,000 messages per day if every user action triggers a job.

entries.name: cron-job.org
entries.free: Free scheduled HTTP calls, as often as once per minute, with execution history and failure notifications.
entries.hitsFirst: Your endpoint must be public and should check a secret, or anyone can trigger it.

entries.name: GitHub Actions
entries.free: Standard runners in public repositories are free. Private repositories on GitHub Free get $12 of included compute per month (about 2,000 Linux minutes at $0.006 per minute) and 500 MB of artifact storage.
entries.hitsFirst: Private-repo minutes once you add tests, previews and scheduled jobs.

entries.name: Tally
entries.free: Forms and submissions with no fixed cap (fair-usage guidelines apply), payments, file uploads, webhooks and integrations.
entries.hitsFirst: Tally branding and no custom domain on free.

entries.name: Formspree (Free)
entries.free: Form backend for static sites: 50 submissions per month.
entries.hitsFirst: 50 submissions per month, and the dashboard only shows the last 30 days.

entries.name: Crisp (Free)
entries.free: Website chat widget and shared inbox with 2 seats.
entries.hitsFirst: No AI credits on free, and 2 seats.

entries.name: Stripe
entries.free: No setup or monthly fees; standard US card pricing is 2.9% + 30¢ per successful charge.
entries.hitsFirst: Not free, pay-per-transaction: model fees into your price before launch.
